schema_note: Custom format, composed in this thread because the architect skill's canonical templates (questions/, knowledge/, templates/) weren't available in this session's environment. A fresh Claude Code session can read this file directly and move task by task respecting depends_on and status, with or without the /architect-next command.
ordering_rule: Don't start a phase without closing the previous one, in principle — in practice the owner has repeatedly asked to build camera-independent phase-2+ work ahead of phase 1 (tasks 2.1-2.12 all shipped before phase 1 closed), which is now known to be the right call: per RUMBO.md's 2026-09-11 correction, the camera plugin is a real technical risk worth prototyping early, but its failure no longer 'invalidates the project' the way this rule used to claim — see RUMBO.md, 'The technical risk that goes first'.

tasks.title: Capacitor project scaffold
tasks.description: React 19.2.8 + TypeScript + Vite 8.0.9 + Zustand 5.0.15, wrapped in Capacitor 8.5 (adopts UIScene). Add the iOS platform. Check the TypeScript version with `npm view typescript version` at install time — deliberately unpinned in this document, resolved in the moment.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN `npx cap open ios` is run and the app is built on a physical device THE SYSTEM SHALL show the app's blank screen with no native build errors.
tasks.verify_command: npm run build && npx cap sync ios
tasks.verify_note: The Xcode build itself is confirmed by opening the project and running on a device — there's no way to automate that part with a command that exits 0. Automated part (verify_command) passes as of 2026-08-16; opening in Xcode and running on hardware is still open, no device access from this environment.

tasks.title: Native camera plugin skeleton
tasks.description: Custom Capacitor plugin (Swift) that wraps AVFoundation directly — not `@capacitor/camera`. Just the capture session and one call that takes a photo without fine control yet; it's the scaffolding, not the full functionality.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the plugin method is called from JS THE SYSTEM SHALL return an image captured by AVFoundation, visible in the app.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on a physical device — mandatory, the simulator has no real camera (see CLAUDE.md). Code written as of 2026-08-16 (CameraCapturePlugin.swift/.m + the JS wrapper and a manual test button in App.tsx) but not yet built or run on hardware — no Xcode/device access from this environment.

tasks.title: Lock exposure/focus/white balance across frames
tasks.description: The part that actually matters: manually expose the first capture and keep those values fixed (AVCaptureDevice.lockConfiguration, exposureMode/focusMode .locked) for the whole stop-motion session, instead of every photo re-exposing on its own.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN 10 consecutive frames are captured of a static scene under constant light THE SYSTEM SHALL produce 10 images with visually identical exposure and focus to each other — no flicker from auto re-exposure.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification: capture the sequence, play it back at 12fps, confirm by eye there's no flicker. This is the criterion that decides whether the project continues or gets rethought — see RUMBO.md. Code written as of 2026-08-16 (lockCaptureSettings/unlockCaptureSettings on CameraCapturePlugin, KVO-waits for isAdjustingExposure/isAdjustingFocus to settle before locking) plus lock/unlock buttons and a multi-frame filmstrip in the App.tsx test harness — but never compiled or run, no Xcode/device access from this environment. The actual 10-frames-no-flicker check hasn't happened.

phases.name: Local capture + drawing engine, no cloud

tasks.title: Port Trace's core/ pattern, adapted to camera cels
tasks.description: types.ts, math.ts, document.ts, history.ts — same layered design as Trace (no DOM, no React), but a Cel can now originate from a captured photo as well as a drawn stroke.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the engine test suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass with no failures, including a test confirming a camera Cel and a drawn Cel share the same compositing interface.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-08-16 (82/82). Built ahead of 1.3's device verification on explicit owner instruction ("start what you can now, easiest to hardest") — this task doesn't touch native code or WebGL, so it isn't at risk from a camera-plugin rethink the way 2.2+ would be. Trimmed from Trace's document.ts on purpose, not by oversight: no rig/skeleton, sprite-swap, text layers, adjustment layers, layer masks, layer groups, or audio track — none are in Clumsyloop's v1 scope (see CLAUDE.md). LayerKind is 'camera' | 'draw' instead of Trace's 'draw' | 'reference' | 'adjustment' — that split is the actual product differentiator.

tasks.title: WebGL2 renderer: compositing camera frame + drawn layers
tasks.description: gl/renderer.ts — upload the captured photo as a texture, composite it with the drawing layers on top, all alpha-premultiplied. A single Y-flip pass, same as Trace.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a document with a camera Cel and a drawn Cel on top is rendered THE SYSTEM SHALL show both composited correctly, with no color halos or orientation mismatch.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-07. Visual verification done headlessly (Playwright + SwiftShader, this environment has no physical device either) via a new RendererHarness component (window.__clumsyloop) and scripts/renderer-smoke.mjs, reading back with renderer.toImageData() rather than a canvas screenshot — same preserveDrawingBuffer:false trap Trace's CLAUDE.md documents. Checks a four-quadrant synthetic photo (catches an orientation flip a solid color couldn't) with a real StrokeBuilder-generated pencil stroke composited on top: all four quadrants keep their own color, the stroke reads clearly darker than the photo under it, and the area just beside the stroke matches the plain photo color with no dark fringe. A screenshot for human eyeballing confirms the same by eye. Trimmed hard from Trace's renderer.ts, all flagged in gl/renderer.ts's own header comment: no GPU texture residency budget/eviction (a real concern for 'hundreds of photos' per RUMBO.md, deliberately deferred until the capture UI, task 2.3, produces real frame counts to profile against instead of guessing), no mesh skinning/rig, no adjustment layers, no selection, no pigment-mix wet blending (one ported brush.ts preset sets pigmentMix, but live stroke merging is the future drawing UI's job), no thumbnail downscaling (task 2.3 is the first actual caller). Kept in full: all 13 BlendModes and brush stamping (drawStamps), since types.ts/brush.ts already commit to them.

tasks.title: Capture UI: onion skin, shutter, filmstrip
tasks.description: Main capture screen — shutter button that calls the native plugin, onion-skin overlay of the previous frame, filmstrip thumbnail strip.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps the shutter THE SYSTEM SHALL add a new frame to the filmstrip and update the onion skin to show that frame as a reference for the next one.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Local export to .mp4 with watermark on the free plan
tasks.description: Encode the full filmstrip (camera + composited drawing layers) to .mp4 via AVFoundation. Watermark gated on entitlement state — which doesn't exist yet at this phase, so for now the free plan is always assumed.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a project of at least 3 frames is exported THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a .mp4 file playable outside the app, with the watermark visible.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification: open the exported .mp4 in another app.

tasks.title: Local project persistence
tasks.description: Save/resume a project (frames + layers + metadata) on local disk, no network. A stop-motion project is hundreds of photos — specifically test that closing and reopening the app loses nothing.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the app is closed mid capture session and reopened THE SYSTEM SHALL restore the project exactly as it was, frame by frame.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-08. Built ahead of 2.3 (capture UI) on explicit owner instruction, same kind of exception as 2.1/2.2: persistence logic doesn't touch the camera plugin or need a real shutter button to exercise it, only a document with cels in it (synthetic ones here, same reasoning as the 2.2 harness). 2.4 (export) was intentionally NOT started alongside this — it needs native AVFoundation/Swift work that shares phase 1's device-verification limitation (can write the code, can't build or run it from this environment), whereas 2.5 is fully browser/IndexedDB-based and testable here. IndexedDB chosen over Capacitor's Filesystem plugin (the owner's call) to avoid a new native dependency for v1; flagged as a real device-reliability question worth another look once actual on-device behavior can be observed. PNG encode/decode uses upng-js (already the library RUMBO.md's known-debts note pointed at) instead of Trace's canvas.toBlob() specifically so core/io.ts runs under npm test (no DOM/canvas in Node) — found and worked around a real decode bug in upng-js@2.1.0 along the way (auto-selected palette mode crashes toRGBA8; forced off via encode's undocumented 6th argument, forbidPlte). Split three ways per CLAUDE.md's gl/-is-the-only-WebGL-contact rule: core/io.ts (pure metadata + PNG, unit tested, 9 new tests in io.test.ts), gl/projectIO.ts (Surface <-> pixels glue), state/projectStore.ts (IndexedDB, degrades to a no-op under Node same as palettes.ts does for localStorage). Verified in a real browser via scripts/persistence-smoke.mjs (Playwright): save a synthetic two-cel-camera-layer + one-draw-layer project, reload the page (the closest proxy this environment has for force-quit + relaunch — no physical device), confirm every field and every composited pixel survives. Along the way this also caught and fixed a real aliasing bug in Renderer.renderDocumentFrame (task 2.2): its returned surface is a reused scratch buffer, so holding two frames' results at once silently corrupts the first — now documented on the method itself, not just fixed locally.

tasks.title: Drawing UI: canvas, pointer input, brush/color panels
tasks.description: Connect the already-ported brush.ts and the curated palettes to a real interactive canvas — pointer events (mouse/pen/touch) drive StrokeBuilder, stamps paint onto the active layer's cel via drawStamps, the result composites and presents live. Not originally itemized in this document (added retroactively on 2026-09-09): checkpoint.md's 2026-08-16 entry already flagged brush.ts as groundwork ported with no consumer yet, and this is that consumer. Single fixed draw layer, single frame — no timeline, no camera layer (that's 2.3, still blocked on device verification).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user drags a pointer across the canvas THE SYSTEM SHALL paint a visible stroke with the selected brush and color, and THE SYSTEM SHALL let the user switch brush or color between strokes without affecting ink already on the canvas.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-09. Owner asked what else could be added while phase 1 stays blocked; this was picked over two other camera-independent options (Firestore rules, the web half of export) as the highest-value one — the actual product differentiator, not backend plumbing. New gl/engine.ts is deliberately minimal, not a port of Trace's core/engine.ts: no revision/touch()/subscribe pub-sub (CLAUDE.md's documented pattern) yet, since the canvas is the only consumer so far and updates itself imperatively after every mutation — add the pub-sub once a second UI piece (layers panel, frame counter) actually needs to react to engine state, not before. No wet-stroke staging surface either (stamps go straight onto the permanent cel); no pigment-mix blending for the one brush.ts preset that wants it (Watercolor); no undo — all real, deliberate simplifications for this first slice, not oversights. Added erase-mode support to Renderer.drawStamps (blendFunc(ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) instead of the normal src-over) since brush.ts's two eraser presets need it and nothing had exercised that path yet. New state/tool.ts (active brush id + color, Zustand) split out the same way palettes.ts already is. Verified with real pointer events (not synthetic Stamp arrays) via scripts/drawing-smoke.mjs (Playwright): draws an actual stroke, confirms it's dark ink not blank paper; switches color and draws again, confirms the new stroke is the new color AND the earlier stroke is byte-for-byte unaffected; switches to the eraser brush and confirms it removes ink; confirms Clear resets the layer. All three Playwright smoke tests (renderer/persistence/drawing) still pass together — no regressions.

tasks.title: Bucket fill tool: tolerance, edge expansion, gap closure, reference-layer fill
tasks.description: Flood fill on the active draw layer, seeded at a tapped point: tolerance decides how different a color can still count as 'inside'; the fill bleeds a few pixels past the line to cover antialiasing (edge expansion/bleed); a real small break in the line doesn't leak the fill out (gap closure); the boundary is read from the whole composited document (any visible layer's ink), so one layer's lineart can bound a fill painted onto a different, active layer (reference-layer fill). Not originally itemized in this document (added 2026-09-10, owner request based on a reference video) — ported and extended from Trace's core/flood.ts + workers/floodFill.worker.ts.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps inside a closed ink outline with the bucket tool THE SYSTEM SHALL fill the enclosed area with the selected color, respecting the outline's edge; WHEN the outline has a small real gap THE SYSTEM SHALL still contain the fill instead of leaking past it; WHEN the active layer differs from the layer holding the outline THE SYSTEM SHALL still bound the fill by that outline while writing only to the active layer.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-10. Ported core/flood.ts near-verbatim from Trace (floodMatch, growFilled/edge-expansion, applyFillColor, extractRect) — but Trace's own shipped bucket tool turns out to only have tolerance + edge expansion, no actual gap closure: growFilled only grows the FILLED region after the fact, it never stops a flood from leaking through a real break in the line in the first place. Since gap closure was one of the two features explicitly asked for, built it for real rather than silently shipping half of what was asked: buildWallMask (inverse of floodMatch's tolerance test) + closeGaps (a genuine morphological close — iterated 3x3 dilate then erode, same iterative-radius style growFilled already uses) + floodOpenMask (scanline fill over the closed wall) — a real pipeline addition beyond what Trace has, not a redesign of what was ported. Renderer gained writeRect (sub-rectangle GPU write-back, sibling to the existing readRect). Engine.floodFill reads the reference from the whole composited frame (not just the active layer), so ink on any visible layer bounds the fill — the reference-layer-fill behavior — while writing only to the active layer's cel; Engine.activeLayerId, previously readonly, gained a setActiveLayer() method purely so this could be exercised at all (DrawingCanvas still only ever has one layer — no layers panel yet to pick an active one, a named UI gap, not a hidden one). No undo, consistent with the rest of the engine (see 2.6). Verified: 11 new core/flood.ts unit tests (including a synthetic case proving a real 1px gap leaks without closure and is contained with it) plus a new scripts/bucket-smoke.mjs driving real pointer-drawn outlines through the actual UI — basic containment, a real ~3px gap contained by default gapClose and proven to leak with gapClose=0, and a two-layer reference-fill scenario reading pixels off each layer's own cel directly. Building this smoke test surfaced and fixed two real bugs, neither a flood-fill defect: the UI's fill is fire-and-forget (async Worker round trip) so checks must poll the filled cel's surface.version instead of checking immediately or sleeping a guess; and brush.ts's ported One Euro smoothing filter has genuine steady-state lag behind constant-velocity motion, so a scripted drag that stops moving right at its target undershoots by several pixels — fixed by having the test dwell at each stroke's endpoint (a real hand naturally slows down there), not by changing the brush engine. All three prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, build, and lint all clean.

tasks.title: Undo/redo for strokes, bucket fills, and Clear
tasks.description: Wire the already-ported core/history.ts (task 2.1, unused until now) into gl/engine.ts so every mutating action on the active layer's cel — a drawn stroke, a bucket fill, Clear — is undoable and redoable, with UI buttons showing the pending action's label and standard keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl+Y). Not originally itemized in this document (added 2026-09-11, owner picked it over a layers panel or device verification as the next task).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user draws a stroke, fills an area, or clears the layer THE SYSTEM SHALL let them undo that action via button or keyboard shortcut and redo it afterward, restoring the exact prior pixels; WHEN a new action happens after an undo THE SYSTEM SHALL discard the redo stack.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Engine.beginStroke snapshots the whole active cel once (readRect over the full document) before any stamp is painted, then tracks only the dirty rect actually touched (expandRect per stamp, same padding Trace uses) so the Command stores just that sub-rectangle's before/after via extractRect — not the full cel — keeping undo memory proportional to what actually changed. This is coarser than Trace's own undo, which snapshots only the stroke's dirty rect from the start because it draws to a wet staging surface until pointer-up; this engine (task 2.6) stamps straight onto the permanent cel with no wet layer, so there's no untouched 'before' surface to read a precise rect from mid-stroke — a real, documented consequence of that earlier simplification, not an oversight here. Bucket fill uses history.run() (the action hasn't executed yet, unlike a stroke which already has by endStroke) with before/after computed from the flood worker's own returned sub-rect. Clear does a simple full-cel snapshot. A layer's cel is only created lazily (ensureCel, mirroring Trace's {cel, created} pattern) so undoing an action that created the first cel on an empty layer removes it entirely, not just paints it blank. UI: Undo/Redo buttons show the pending command's label (history.undoLabel/redoLabel) and disable correctly; DrawingCanvas subscribes to history.subscribe() inside the same effect that creates the Engine (a plain useState counter, not useSyncExternalStore — avoids a real ordering hazard where useSyncExternalStore's internal subscribe effect can fire before a separate effect that creates the subscribable object, missing the subscription on first mount). Bugs caught while building this: a self-caught no-op ternary in endStroke's label logic (read this.strokeBrush AFTER already nulling it a few lines above); a proactively-avoided ArrayBuffer detachment bug (postMessage's zero-copy transfer of target.buffer would have destroyed floodFill's own pre-fill snapshot had target.slice() not been taken before the transfer, not after). Verified via a new scripts/undo-smoke.mjs (Playwright): real pointer-drawn strokes, a real bucket fill, and Clear, each undone and redone through the actual UI (buttons and keyboard alike) — two independent strokes undo/redo in the correct order, a new stroke after an undo discards the redo stack, and a bucket fill's undo/redo round-trips correctly. Building it surfaced a test-methodology issue, not a product bug: the 'marker' brush preset is a chisel tip (aspect: 0.35), so its actual cross-stroke width is size(28) * aspect ≈ 9.8px, not the full 28px diameter assumed at first — a wide averaging box around the sample point was washing the thin line's darkness out into false negatives on presence checks; fixed by shrinking the sampling window to fit inside the known stroke width for presence checks specifically (same reasoning bucket-smoke.mjs already uses a small half for thin ink, e.g. checking the fineliner outline itself), while leaving the wider window on blank-paper checks since a wide box over empty paper is still reliably blank. All four prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Layers panel: add, delete, reorder, rename, visibility, lock, active-layer selection
tasks.description: UI to actually use the multi-layer document model that's existed since task 2.1 but had no way to exercise beyond a single fixed layer and a test harness calling setActiveLayer() by hand. Add/delete layers, reorder the stack, rename, toggle visibility and lock, and pick which layer strokes/fills write into. Not originally itemized in this document (owner picked it 2026-09-11, alongside starting Firebase and addressing engine drawing debts, all requested together — this is the first of the three).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user adds a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL make it the active one; WHEN the user deletes a layer (with more than one remaining) THE SYSTEM SHALL remove it and fall back to another active layer; WHEN the user hides a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it from the composite while leaving its pixels intact; WHEN the user locks a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse both strokes and fills on it; WHEN the user reorders layers THE SYSTEM SHALL update the composite stacking order; WHEN only one layer remains THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to delete it.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Engine gained addLayer/removeLayer/moveLayer/setLayerVisible/setLayerLocked/renameLayer, all 'draw'-only (a camera layer's cels only ever come from the still device-blocked capture UI, task 2.3, so there's nothing meaningful for a panel button to add). removeLayer calls renderer.release() on each of the removed layer's cel surfaces immediately, since — unlike stroke/fill undo — layer removal isn't undoable, so nothing can still need that GPU texture afterward; this sidesteps a real gap that already exists elsewhere in the engine (a stroke/fill's created-cel undo keeps its Surface reachable for redo but never explicitly frees the GPU texture once the History entry itself gets trimmed by MAX_STEPS/MAX_BYTES — a pre-existing leak from tasks 2.6-2.8, not introduced here, and still open). Structural layer operations (add/remove/reorder/rename/visibility/lock) deliberately have no undo, unlike strokes/fills/Clear (task 2.8): a bare layer has no pixels for undo to meaningfully restore, and adding Command-based undo for array-splice operations on top of GPU-resource-holding Layer objects would reopen the same disposal-timing problem removeLayer's immediate release() was specifically added to avoid. This is also the point where CLAUDE.md's documented touch()/revision/subscribe() pattern (deferred at every engine.ts revision since task 2.6, each time noting there was no second consumer yet to justify it) finally gets built: the layers panel is that second consumer, and touch() lives inside renderAndPresent() itself (called at the end of every mutation already) rather than being sprinkled through every mutator by hand. Building this surfaced a real, separate bug worth its own line: Engine.beginStroke never checked layer.locked or layer.visible at all — only floodFill did (task 2.7) — so locking a layer through the new panel would have silently done nothing for strokes; fixed by adding the same guard beginStroke already needed on principle, not just to make the new UI feature work. Verified via a new scripts/layers-smoke.mjs (Playwright) covering: starting state (one active layer); add-layer making the new layer active; clicking a layer row to switch active layer; a stroke landing on whichever layer is active; rename via double-click-to-edit; hide/show actually removing/restoring a layer from the composite; lock genuinely blocking a stroke (not just a fill); reorder changing composite order; delete removing a layer and being refused (both via the disabled button and by calling removeLayer() directly) once only one layer remains. All five prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Wet-stroke staging surface for non-erase strokes
tasks.description: Closes the drawing-engine debt flagged since task 2.6: stamps for a non-erase stroke now land on a scratch 'wet' surface for the whole stroke (composited live on top of the active layer's cel for the canvas preview) and only merge onto the permanent cel at endStroke, matching Trace's own approach, instead of painting straight onto the permanent cel as they arrive. Not originally itemized in this document (owner asked for this alongside the layers panel and starting Firebase, 2026-09-11; this is the second of the three, picked over also building pigment-mix blending itself in the same pass — see verify_note).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user drags a non-erase stroke THE SYSTEM SHALL show it live on the canvas before the pointer lifts, without creating a cel on a previously-empty layer until the stroke actually ends; WHEN the pointer lifts THE SYSTEM SHALL merge the stroke onto the permanent cel with the same final pixels as before this change; WHEN the user erases THE SYSTEM SHALL continue to affect the permanent cel directly, unaffected by the wet surface.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Renderer.renderDocumentFrame gained an optional wetOverlay param ({layerId, surface}), threaded into rasterizeLayer: when given and it names the layer being rasterized, that layer's cel (or a clear scratch surface, if the layer has no cel yet — the brand-new-layer case) gets `drawOver`'d with the wet surface into a scratch before taking part in the rest of the composite, using the renderer's existing copy/drawOver primitives — no new shader needed. Engine.beginStroke/paintStamps/endStroke branch on `!brush.erase`: non-erase stamps go to `renderer.scratch('wetStroke')` and only `drawOver` onto the real cel (lazily created via ensureCel, only if the stroke actually painted something) at endStroke; erase stamps still go straight onto the permanent cel throughout, unchanged from before this task, because erase's `blendFunc(ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)` punches a hole in whatever is already there — routing it through an initially-transparent wet surface would erase nothing, then a normal drawOver merge would silently undo the whole gesture. This is exactly why Trace itself, and now this engine, don't put erase through wet staging either. A real, welcome side effect: undo's dirty-rect 'before' snapshot for a non-erase stroke can now be read right at endStroke, immediately before the merge, instead of reading the whole cel at beginStroke the way task 2.8 had to (the erase path still needs the old whole-cel read, since it never had an untouched pre-stroke surface to read from later). Standard alpha-blend compositing is associative for premultiplied 'over', so merging N stamps' accumulated wet-surface result onto the cel in one drawOver produces bit-identical pixels to painting the same N stamps directly onto the cel in sequence — confirmed by the unchanged pixel values across every pre-existing Playwright smoke test after this change, not just their pass/fail status. Pigment-mix blending (BrushPreset.pigmentMix, the MIX_FS shader gl/shaders.ts's own header comment already flagged as intentionally unbuilt) is still NOT implemented — this task only builds the wet-staging plumbing a future MIX_FS pass needs to hook into at the merge step; today's merge is plain drawOver regardless of pigmentMix, so Watercolor's pigmentMix: 0.15 still has no visible effect, exactly as before. Verified via a new scripts/wet-stroke-smoke.mjs (Playwright): a brand-new layer with no cel previews a stroke live before pointer-up and still has no cel mid-stroke; the stroke is visible both mid-drag and after merge; the permanent cel is created only by the merge; the eraser is confirmed to still act on the permanent cel mid-stroke (unaffected by wet staging). All six prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified with pixel values essentially unchanged (not just passing) — direct evidence the associativity argument holds in practice, not just in theory; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Visual pass on the drawing screen (dark theme, icons, layout)
tasks.description: Every control in DrawingCanvas/LayersPanel had been default unstyled HTML since task 2.6 — deliberate, since all effort up to now went into the engine (rendering, brushes, undo, layers, wet strokes), not the chrome around it. Owner tested the web preview on a phone (2026-09-11), compared it unfavorably to a TikTok ad demoing Procreate's own Animation Assist ('parece Paint muy antiguo'), and while that specific comparison wasn't apples to apples (a 10+-year-old paid professional app vs. a weeks-old prototype with camera capture still unbuilt), the underlying point was fair: the unstyled test harness made it hard to actually judge the drawing experience. Not originally itemized (added retroactively 2026-09-11, same day as 2.9/2.10, in direct response to that feedback).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the drawing screen loads THE SYSTEM SHALL present a dark, app-like layout (icon-labeled controls, consistent card sections, a segmented Draw/Bucket control, circular color swatches) instead of unstyled default HTML controls; WHEN the same screen is tested THE SYSTEM SHALL behave identically to before this task — no functional or engine change, and every existing test selector (button accessible names, aria-labels, DOM structure) SHALL keep working unmodified.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Pure CSS/JSX restyle, zero engine changes: new src/ui/drawing.css (plain CSS, not Tailwind — no such dependency exists yet and one screen doesn't justify adding one; dark palette keyed off #17171a/#121214 to match gl/renderer.ts's own WebGL clear color so the page doesn't clash with the canvas) and src/ui/icons.tsx (hand-authored inline SVG icons — no icon-library dependency, no emoji per the project's own UI-copy conventions; every icon is aria-hidden so it never contributes to a button's accessible name). Verified the accessible-name invariant explicitly before touching anything, not just hoped it held: enumerated every getByRole/aria-label lookup across all 7 Playwright smoke scripts, found the hard constraints (canvas id="drawing-canvas"; button name exactly "Clear"; button names matching /^Undo/ and /^Redo/; LayersPanel's "{verb} {layer.name}" aria-labels for Hide/Show/Lock/Unlock/Move up/Move down/Delete; "Add layer" exact match; <li><span> layer-row structure; <li input> for renaming), and preserved every one of them while restyling — icon+label buttons keep their original text so accessible names are unchanged, aria-label-driven buttons keep the exact same aria-label. Also collapsed the camera-plugin/renderer/persistence dev harnesses in ui/App.tsx behind a <details> (closed by default) — they were the other big contributor to the 'looks like an old program' impression, sitting directly below the drawing screen in raw unstyled HTML; left functionally untouched, just no longer competing for attention by default. Discovered and fixed a real gap while wiring the CSS import: this project had no src/vite-env.d.ts, so `tsc -b` couldn't type-check a `.css` side-effect import at all (`import './drawing.css'` failed with TS2882) — added the standard Vite scaffold file (`/// <reference types="vite/client" />`), which was simply always missing since this project never imported a non-TS asset before this task. Verified with a real screenshot (Playwright, both Draw and Bucket modes) before shipping, not just by reading the CSS — confirmed card sections, the segmented control's active state, circular swatches with a selection ring, and the brush chip rows' horizontal scroll with a fade-out mask hinting more content, all render as intended. All 7 Playwright smoke tests (renderer/persistence/drawing/bucket/undo/layers/wet-stroke) re-verified with no regressions — none of their selectors needed updating; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Responsive layout: canvas stays fixed and visible across phone/iPad/desktop
tasks.description: Owner tested 2.11's visual pass and raised two real, distinct problems, not just taste: (1) picking a color scrolled the canvas itself out of view, which no real drawing app does; (2) the layout was hard-capped at 480px width, so it wasted almost the whole screen on iPad or desktop instead of adapting. Not originally itemized (added retroactively 2026-09-11, same conversation as 2.11, in direct response to that follow-up feedback).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user scrolls the Layers/Tool/Brush/Color panel on any screen size THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the canvas, status text, and Undo/Redo/Clear toolbar fully visible and unaffected; WHEN the viewport is tablet or desktop width THE SYSTEM SHALL use the extra space (canvas grows, panel becomes a sidebar) instead of centering a phone-width column in empty space; WHEN the same drawing/undo/layers behavior is tested THE SYSTEM SHALL be unaffected — no engine change.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. `.cl-app` became a fixed-height (100dvh) flex column that never scrolls itself; `.cl-main` splits into `.cl-canvas-col` (canvas + status + toolbar, sized top-down from `.cl-main`'s definite height, never by its own content) and `.cl-panels` (the ONLY scrolling region, capped at 42vh on narrow screens so the canvas can never be scrolled away). At >=700px, `.cl-main` switches from a column to a row: canvas gets the majority of a much wider stage and `.cl-panels` becomes an independently-scrolling sidebar. The canvas itself gained `object-fit: contain` (it has a fixed intrinsic 360x640 bitmap — DrawingCanvas.tsx's DOC_WIDTH/DOC_HEIGHT — and a replaced element never grows past its intrinsic size without an explicit display size, so without this it would sit tiny in a sea of empty space on any screen bigger than its native resolution). Two real bugs found and fixed while building this, both caught by actually running the test suite rather than trusting the CSS reasoning alone: (1) `.cl-canvas-col` was initially `flex: none` (sized bottom-up by its own content) instead of `flex: 1` (sized top-down from the parent's definite height) — meaning the canvas's rendered size could shift when sibling text changed width (e.g. "Undo" becoming "Undo (Stroke)" once there was something to undo), silently invalidating any pointer coordinate a test had cached before that point; undo-smoke's second and third stroke checks failed this way before the fix. (2) object-fit:contain means the canvas's CSS box and its actually-rendered content can legitimately have different aspect ratios (letterboxing) depending on available space — DrawingCanvas.tsx's own toSample() needed a real coordinate-math fix to recover the true letterboxed content rect (mirroring how object-fit:contain itself computes it) instead of a naive canvasBox.width/height linear scale, and every Playwright smoke script's own toScreen() helper (bucket/drawing/layers/undo/wet-stroke-smoke, all sharing the same copy-pasted pattern) needed the identical fix, since they compute click targets independently and must agree with the app's own transform. Verified with real screenshots at phone (390x844), iPad (834x1194), and desktop (1440x900) widths, plus one explicitly scrolling the panel to confirm the canvas stays put — not just by reading the CSS. All 7 Playwright smoke tests, 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Layout rearchitecture: full-bleed canvas with floating rails and panels
tasks.description: 2.12's docked-panel approach (canvas + toolbar in one flex column, a capped-height scrolling panel beside/below it) still meant the canvas had to permanently share layout space with the panel and shrink to make room for it — not what any real drawing/animation app (including this project's own Trace) actually does. Directly requested by the owner after reviewing Trace and two other sibling repos (draw, Beautyapp) for reference: rebuild the layout to match Trace's real pattern — the canvas fills the entire viewport full-bleed, and small floating translucent 'rail' toolbars plus closeable floating 'panel' overlays sit on top of it, never sharing space with it. Not originally itemized (added 2026-09-11, same session as the 'What Clumsyloop is' correction, chosen over the two smaller alternatives offered — format-picker only, or just the docked-panel label bug fix — as the 'Rearquitecturar el layout (recomendado)' option).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the drawing screen loads on any viewport size THE SYSTEM SHALL show the canvas filling the entire screen (no card/border/padding shrinking it) with floating icon-only rail toolbars overlaid on top; WHEN the user opens the Layers, Brush, or Color panel THE SYSTEM SHALL show it as a closeable floating overlay anchored to one edge, not as a permanently docked sidebar that resizes the canvas; WHEN Escape is pressed or the panel's close button is tapped THE SYSTEM SHALL close it and return the canvas to its full, unobstructed size; WHEN the same drawing/undo/layers/bucket/wet-stroke behavior is tested THE SYSTEM SHALL be unaffected — no engine change.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke && npm run test:renderer-smoke && npm run test:persistence-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Ported the actual reference pattern from Trace's own src/styles.css/controls.tsx/Toolbar.tsx (read directly, not guessed): drawing.css rewritten around `.cl-app` (position:fixed;inset:0, full-viewport), `.cl-canvas` (position:absolute;inset:0;object-fit:contain, no wrapper/card), `.cl-rail`/`.cl-rail--left`/`.cl-rail--top` (small position:absolute translucent/blurred pill toolbars, 40x40 icon-only `.cl-railbtn` buttons), and `.cl-panel` (position:absolute floating overlay card, right-anchored, `top:calc(10px+56px);bottom:10px;width:320px`). Color tokens converged independently close to Trace's own (#131316/#1c1c21/etc.) rather than being copy-pasted, confirmed by reading Trace's actual file. New src/ui/FloatingPanel.tsx (Escape-to-close via a keydown listener, `onPointerDown` stopPropagation so panel interaction doesn't fall through to the canvas underneath) supplies every panel's title bar and close button — Layers/Brush/Color panels no longer render their own headers. Deliberately does NOT port Trace's drag-to-reposition (`useDraggable`) for panels: a fixed right-edge anchor is enough of an improvement over 2.12's docked sidebar on its own, and drag position persistence/off-screen clamping is real extra state not needed to fix the actual complaint. `DrawingCanvas.tsx` gained `activePanel: PanelId | null` state (closed by default) with rail buttons toggling it; Undo/Redo/Clear stayed as always-visible top-rail buttons (not behind a panel) specifically so no existing test needed to change how it reaches them. `LayersPanel.tsx` lost its own section header (redundant now that `FloatingPanel` supplies "Layers" + a close button) but every per-row aria-label and the `<li><span>`/`<li><input>` structure is byte-for-byte unchanged. Two new icons added (icons.tsx): `LayersIcon` (stacked-plane glyph for the Layers rail button) and `CloseIcon` (for `FloatingPanel`'s own close button), following the file's existing aria-hidden/common-stroke-style pattern exactly. Verified against the FULL 7-script Playwright smoke suite, not just the 5 already listed in this task's own verify_command: renderer-smoke and persistence-smoke also re-run and pass, confirming zero engine/rendering regression from a change that touched only ui/. Only one script needed an actual edit: layers-smoke.mjs's Layers panel is now closed by default (a floating overlay, not a permanently-visible section), so its very first UI interaction (clicking "Add layer") timed out until a single `await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Layers' }).click()` was added right after the engine-ready wait to open the panel once at the start of the script — every check after that line was already written against the panel's contents and needed no further change. The other six scripts (renderer/persistence/drawing/bucket/undo/wet-stroke) passed with zero changes, since they all drive brush/mode/color state via `window.__clumsyloopTool`/engine JS calls rather than clicking UI chips, and Undo/Redo/Clear kept their exact pre-existing accessible names as always-visible rail buttons. All 7 Playwright smoke tests, 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Timeline: frame navigation, add/duplicate/delete frame, onion skin, fps
tasks.description: The camera-independent half of what task 2.3 originally bundled as 'onion skin, shutter, filmstrip'. Owner asked to advance everything not blocked on hardware (2026-09-11, following the direction correction below): this is the single biggest remaining camera-independent gap, since the drawing engine was hardcoded to a single implicit frame 0 even though core/document.ts's Cel model (a sparse Map<frame, Cel> per layer) and gl/renderer.ts's renderDocumentFrame(doc, frame) already supported an arbitrary frame — task 2.6's engine simply never exposed it. Also closes two of RUMBO.md's named competitive gaps at once: onion skinning (Callipeg's strength) and a global fps setting (a smaller slice of RoughAnimator's adjustable-FPS strength — see this task's own scope note on what's deliberately NOT covered).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user steps to the next/previous frame THE SYSTEM SHALL move the playhead and show that frame's own composited content; WHEN the user adds a new frame THE SYSTEM SHALL create a blank cel on the active layer right after the current frame and jump to it, growing the document's frame count if needed; WHEN the user duplicates a frame THE SYSTEM SHALL copy the currently-held cel's pixels into a new cel at the next frame; WHEN the user deletes a frame THE SYSTEM SHALL remove only a cel that starts exactly at the current frame, falling back to whatever cel was held before it; WHEN any of these actions happens THE SYSTEM SHALL make it undoable and redoable; WHEN onion skin is enabled THE SYSTEM SHALL show the previous frame as a faint ghost underneath the current one without altering any actual cel pixels; WHEN the fps field is edited THE SYSTEM SHALL update the document's frame rate.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:timeline-smoke && npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke && npm run test:renderer-smoke && npm run test:persistence-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. gl/engine.ts gained `currentFrame` (private, navigated via `setCurrentFrame`/`stepFrame`), `addCel(duplicate?)` and `deleteCel()` on the active layer, `setOnionSkin(enabled)`, and `setFps(fps)` — none of it needed a renderer change: `ensureCel`/`beginStroke`/`clearActiveLayer`/`floodFill` were generalized from a hardcoded frame 0 to a `frame` parameter (defaulting to `currentFrame`, but captured once into a local at the start of a stroke/fill so a frame change mid-action, which `setCurrentFrame` already prevents by ending any in-progress stroke first, can't retarget where the action writes). `addCel`/`deleteCel` mirror Trace's own `addCel`/`deleteCel` semantics exactly (read from its `core/engine.ts` directly, not guessed): `addCel` targets `currentFrame + 1`, copies the currently-held cel's pixels when duplicating, grows `doc.frameCount` only if the target frame doesn't already fit (reversed by the same undo command so undo never leaves the timeline longer than before), and simply navigates instead of overwriting if a cel already exists at the target frame; `deleteCel` only removes a cel that starts exactly at `currentFrame` (not whichever cel is currently held, which could have started several frames earlier) — both undoable via `history.run`, unlike the layers panel's structural operations (task 2.9), since a frame can carry real pixels worth restoring. Onion skin (`Engine.renderAndPresent`'s new branch) needed zero renderer changes either: it renders the previous frame via the SAME `renderDocumentFrame(doc, frame)` the current frame already uses, with `paperAlpha` forced to 0 on a shallow-cloned doc object (not a renderer parameter) so the paper is only painted once as the accumulator's base, then `drawOver`s the ghost at a fixed 0.35 opacity before drawing the current frame on top at full opacity — the renderer's existing `scratch()`/`drawOver()`/`fill()` primitives already supported everything needed. Deliberately narrower than Trace's own onion skin: one frame back only (not separately configurable before/after counts), a fixed opacity (not user-adjustable), and no tinted ghost color (Trace's `composite()` supports a `tint` option this renderer doesn't have) — a richer onion-skin panel is real future work, not an oversight, and this covers the single most common case (checking the immediately preceding pose) that actually unblocks drawing a walk cycle or a simple loop today. Similarly, `setFps` is a single document-wide frame rate, not Callipeg/RoughAnimator's true per-frame hold-duration control — that's a materially bigger feature (variable-length holds per cel) deliberately deferred, not silently claimed as done. New `src/ui/Timeline.tsx` (prev/next frame, frame counter, new/duplicate/delete-frame buttons, onion-skin toggle, fps input) mounted as a new bottom-center `.cl-rail--bottom`, following the exact same `engine.subscribe()`-in-`useEffect` pattern `LayersPanel` already established, always visible (not behind a panel toggle, unlike Layers/Brush/Color) since frame navigation is core to using the app at all. Deliberately NOT a filmstrip: rendering a thumbnail per frame would mean rasterizing every frame to a small canvas on every mutation, and text-based frame count/navigation is enough to be useful without that cost — a real filmstrip is future work. Four new icons (icons.tsx): StepBackIcon/StepForwardIcon/DuplicateFrameIcon/OnionIcon, following the file's existing pattern. `DrawingCanvas.tsx`'s initial `newDocument` call changed from a hardcoded single frame (`frameCount: 1`, which made a timeline meaningless) to the module's own stated default of 24. Verified via a new scripts/timeline-smoke.mjs: frame isolation (drawing on one frame doesn't touch another, checked by reading `renderDocumentFrame(doc, frame)` directly per frame — ground truth, unaffected by onion either way); duplicate frame actually copies pixels; delete frame falls back to the previously-held cel; undo/redo across a sequence of frame actions restores both cel presence and frame count correctly; onion skin verified by reading back the renderer's own `'onionAcc'` scratch surface directly (the exact surface fed into `present()`) rather than the presented canvas — sidesteps the same live-canvas-readback unreliability CLAUDE.md already flags for WebGL content with `preserveDrawingBuffer:false`, and confirms a real, non-blank ghost pixel where only the previous frame has ink, while the current frame's own data at that point stays confirmed-blank throughout. Building this test surfaced the same thin-brush-averaging issue undo-smoke.mjs already documented for the default 'marker' preset (now the default first brush, `size: 6`): a wide sampling box around a thin stroke washes out its darkness into false negatives — fixed the same way, by shrinking the sampling window for solid-ink presence checks specifically. Also caught and fixed a real narrow-viewport layout gap while screenshot-verifying: the new bottom timeline rail overflowed a 390px-wide phone screen enough to clip the fps input's unit label at the very edge — tightened `.cl-frame-counter`/`.cl-fps-input` padding and shrank the fps field from 44px to 32px, confirmed by re-screenshotting; the row still sits right at the edge on the narrowest phones, a known remaining polish item, not a functional gap (the input itself is fully visible and usable, verified interactively via the smoke test at a slightly wider 500px test viewport). All 8 Playwright smoke tests, 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Firebase project + Sign in with Apple
tasks.description: Create the Firebase project, Firebase Auth with Sign in with Apple as the primary method (capacitor-firebase, current verified plugins: messaging 8.3.0, analytics 8.3.0, firestore 8.1.0 — confirm the current version at install time).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps 'Sign in with Apple' THE SYSTEM SHALL create or recover their account and leave them authenticated in Firebase Auth.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device — Sign in with Apple doesn't work in every simulator environment.

tasks.title: Firestore schema: users, projects, entitlements
tasks.description: Base collections and security rules — each user can only read/write their own projects and their own entitlement, never another user's.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN an authenticated user tries to read another user's entitlement document THE SYSTEM SHALL deny access via Firestore rules.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Built ahead of 3.1 on the same kind of exception already used repeatedly in phase 2 (2.5/2.6/2.7 built ahead of 2.3): 3.1 needs a real Firebase Console project and a physical device for Sign in with Apple, neither available in this environment, but the rules themselves are fully testable against the LOCAL Firestore emulator with no live project at all — `.firebaserc`'s 'demo-clumsyloop' project ID is the documented way to run the emulator suite standalone (Firebase treats any 'demo-*' project ID as emulator-only, never touching real GCP). firestore.rules covers exactly the three collections this task's own title names, not more: users/{userId} (publicly readable — the future feed needs to show a clip's owner — writable only by that user, to their own doc only), projects/{projectId} (read/update/delete gated on the EXISTING document's ownerId via `resource.data`, create gated on the INCOMING one via `request.resource.data`, since `resource` doesn't exist yet on create — a common real mistake in Firestore rules if both checks aren't kept distinct), entitlements/{userId} (read your own, write NONE at all — CLAUDE.md is explicit that only a Cloud Function's Admin-SDK write, which bypasses these rules entirely, is trusted; task 3.4 is what will actually perform that write). Deliberately does NOT add rules for clips/reports (phases 4/5) — those aren't itemized tasks yet, and writing rules for a collection with no defined write path yet would be guessing, not scoping. Added firebase-tools, @firebase/rules-unit-testing, and firebase as devDependencies, plus firebase.json/.firebaserc for the emulator config. Verified via a new scripts/firestore-rules-test.mjs (16 checks against the real emulator, not a rules simulator): public read of a user profile, self-write allowed, cross-user write denied, unauthenticated write denied; project create/read/update/delete allowed for the owner and denied for a different user, including the create-with-spoofed-ownerId case; entitlement read allowed for the owner, denied for a different user, and write denied even for the owner themselves. All 16 pass. tsc, lint, build, and all 131 unit tests remain clean; this task doesn't touch any web app code, only adds emulator-only Firebase config and its own test script.

tasks.title: StoreKit 2 purchase flow (client)
tasks.description: Subscription screen, native StoreKit 2 integration (or equivalent Capacitor plugin) to start the purchase and receive the transaction.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user completes a sandbox purchase THE SYSTEM SHALL receive the client-side transaction signed by StoreKit.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification with an App Store Connect sandbox account.

tasks.title: Cloud Function: receipt validation → entitlement in Firestore
tasks.description: The client transaction is never trusted alone — the Cloud Function validates against the App Store Server API and only then writes the entitlement.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a valid sandbox transaction is sent to the Cloud Function THE SYSTEM SHALL write the entitlement to Firestore; WHEN a tampered or fake transaction is sent THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it without writing anything.

tasks.title: Gate premium features behind the entitlement
tasks.description: Remove the watermark, enable extra layers and cloud save only if the Firestore entitlement is active.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user's entitlement is active THE SYSTEM SHALL export with no watermark; WHEN it isn't THE SYSTEM SHALL keep it.

tasks.title: clips collection in Firestore + Storage upload
tasks.description: Publishing pipeline: upload the exported .mp4 to Firebase Storage, create the `clips` document with the URL and metadata (author, date, no likes/comments fields — not part of v1 scope).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user publishes a clip THE SYSTEM SHALL create a `clips` document whose video URL is publicly accessible.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification — confirm the resulting URL plays back in a separate browser.

tasks.title: Feed UI: chronological list, playback
tasks.description: No ranking, no algorithm — simple chronological order, as decided in RUMBO.md.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the feed is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL show published clips ordered newest to oldest, playable inline.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Publish flow from the export screen
tasks.description: 'Publish' button next to export, which triggers 4.1 without the user having to leave the export flow.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user exports and taps 'Publish' THE SYSTEM SHALL complete the upload and show the clip in the feed with no extra steps.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification.

tasks.title: Native share sheet to external networks
tasks.description: UIActivityViewController (via Capacitor's Share plugin) with the .mp4 and a prefilled caption including the app's hashtag, targeting Instagram/TikTok/X/Threads/Facebook — no per-platform API integration.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps 'Share' THE SYSTEM SHALL open the native iOS share sheet with the video attached and the hashtag already written in the text.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Report button + reports collection
tasks.description: Any clip in the feed can be reported. The report stores who, which clip, and a reason.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a user reports a clip THE SYSTEM SHALL create a `reports` document referencing that clip.

tasks.title: Cloud Function: report → hide clip from feed
tasks.description: Once a report threshold is crossed (to be defined, start conservative — 1 report is enough to hide while under review, not to delete), the clip stops appearing in feed queries without being deleted yet.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a clip reaches the report threshold THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it from the query that feeds the public feed.

tasks.title: Minimal internal review panel
tasks.description: Simple web page, protected by Firebase Auth with an admin allowlist, to view reported clips and decide: restore or permanently delete. Not a product — the minimum needed to meet Apple's requirement of acting within 24 hours.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN an admin deletes a reported clip from the panel THE SYSTEM SHALL remove it from Firestore and Storage, not just hide it.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification.

phases.name: Packaging and submission for Apple review

tasks.title: App Store Connect listing
tasks.description: Screenshots, description, privacy labels (Apple requires declaring what data is collected — camera, photos, user content via Firebase) consistent with what the app actually does.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the App Store Connect privacy form is completed THE SYSTEM SHALL declare every type of data the app actually collects, with no omissions.
tasks.verify_note: Manual review against the code: camera, photos, user identifier, generated content.

tasks.title: UGC guideline compliance checklist
tasks.description: Explicitly confirm, before submitting, that report + block + takedown within 24h (phase 5) are complete and documented — the most common rejection reason for apps with a feed.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN Apple's guideline 1.2 (UGC) checklist is reviewed THE SYSTEM SHALL have evidence for every point (working report, working block, documented takedown process).
tasks.verify_note: Manual review against Apple's current guideline at submission time — it may have changed since this document was written.

tasks.title: TestFlight build
